question: What actually is a research problem in nursing?

options.A: An expensive piece of equipment needed for the intensive care unit
options.B: A personal complaint raised by hospital management staff
options.C: A gap in knowledge or unresolved difficulty requiring investigation
options.D: A final medical diagnosis given by a lead physician

explanation: Think of a research problem as an unanswered question or a puzzle in clinical practice that needs proper study to figure out. You've got this!

question: Why do we need a clear research problem before starting any study?

options.A: It gives the study direction and ensures it adds value to healthcare
options.B: It forces doctors to change their prescription habits
options.C: It removes all need for data collection and statistical analysis
options.D: It guarantees the hospital will receive financial grants immediately

explanation: Having a clear focus keeps your project on track so that your findings actually help improve patient care or nursing knowledge. Great job!

question: Where do bedside nurses usually spot their first research ideas?

options.A: By reading financial audits of hospital pharmacies
options.B: Through political debates in national assemblies
options.C: Inside historical textbooks written decades ago
options.D: During routine patient care observations and shift routines

explanation: As nurses, we see what happens on the ward every single day. Your daily clinical experiences are a goldmine for research topics!

question: A nurse notices morning shift surgical patients report less pain than evening ones. Why is this a good research problem?

options.A: It highlights a noticeable pattern and potential gap in pain management routines
options.B: It proves that evening nurses are performing their duties incorrectly
options.C: It guarantees a promotion for the nurse who records the observation
options.D: It eliminates the need to administer prescribed pain medications

explanation: Spotting differences in patient care across shifts points to a real clinical puzzle worth investigating. You're thinking like a true researcher!

question: In a published research paper, where can you usually find recommendations for future studies?

options.C: At the end of the article

explanation: Researchers love to wrap up their papers by pointing out what still needs to be explored. Always check the conclusion section!

question: How does reading past literature help a nurse choose a new research topic?

options.A: It provides a list of patients who agreed to join the study
options.B: It automatically writes the methodology chapter for the new study
options.C: It proves that all healthcare questions have already been answered
options.D: It helps identify what is still unknown so duplication is avoided

explanation: Checking what others have done saves you from repeating old work and helps you find fresh territory to explore. Keep it up!

question: What is the main reason for using a nursing theory in your research?

options.A: To dictate the exact medication dosage a patient must receive
options.B: To replace the need for ethical approval from the hospital board
options.C: To provide a structured framework for examining patient care
options.D: To calculate the monthly budget for the nursing unit

explanation: Theories act like a pair of glasses, helping us look at patient care in an organized and logical way.

question: A nurse wonders if a self-care theory works for elderly patients in rural farming communities. Where does this research idea come from?
explanation: Testing established nursing models on new groups of people is a fantastic way to grow our professional knowledge.

question: Which of these is a national healthcare priority that often inspires nursing research?

options.A: The interior paint color of the administrative offices
options.B: The brand of stationery used by the hospital secretary
options.C: The personal shoe color preference of ward nurses
options.D: High rates of maternal mortality in rural clinics

explanation: Big public health challenges like maternal mortality are urgent priorities that governments and health workers need to study and solve.

question: Why should nursing researchers care about national and global health goals?

options.A: It helps secure research funding and ensures the study addresses urgent needs
options.B: It removes all ethical considerations from the research process
options.C: It eliminates the requirement to collect informed consent from patients
options.D: It guarantees that no other nurse will ever read the published paper

explanation: When your research tackles pressing real-world problems, it's easier to get support and make a true difference in society.

question: Can everyday communication issues during clinical work spark a good research study?

options.A: Yes, but only if approved by international space agencies first
options.B: Yes, daily interactions and communication issues often reveal systemic flaws
options.C: No, personal experiences are considered too biased to ever be investigated
options.D: No, research problems must come exclusively from laboratory experiments

explanation: Handover hitches and team misunderstandings happen all the time—and they make brilliant starting points for research!

question: A student nurse notices patients often get confused when discharged without written instructions. Why is this a valid research problem?

options.A: It highlights a communication gap that affects patient safety and outcomes
options.B: It proves that patients are entirely at fault for forgetting instructions
options.C: It shows that written paper is more expensive than digital tablets
options.D: It demonstrates that discharge rounds are unnecessary tasks

explanation: Discharge confusion puts patient recovery at risk. Studying how to fix this communication gap is super important for safe nursing!

question: What does 'feasibility' mean when you are checking if a research topic is practical?

options.A: Proving that the research will definitely win an international award
options.B: Ensuring the study topic sounds impressive to senior professors
options.C: Having enough time, money, and resources to complete the study
options.D: Getting permission to skip data collection if things get busy

explanation: Feasibility is just asking: 'Can we realistically pull this study off with the time and materials we have?'

question: A nurse wants to study a rare condition affecting only one person in the country every decade. Which rule does this study break?
explanation: If there aren't enough participants available to study within a reasonable time, the project simply isn't feasible. Spot on!
